 TSM Falls as Chip Selloff Deepens and Export-Control Fears Pressure Sentiment
 By: Quiver PriceTracker
 Posted: 7 hours ago / Nov. 20, 2026 2:45 p.m. UTC 
 TSM
 Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) is down 4.0% today. Here is some analysis on what might have caused this price movement.
 Analysis: The decline appears tied mainly to a broad semiconductor selloff that hit Asian markets hard, with Taiwan equities posting a sharp drop and chip names leading the weakness. Pressure on TSM also likely reflects investor concern that tighter U.S. oversight of advanced chip exports and foundry activity tied to China could weigh on demand visibility and customer activity.
 Details: Taiwan’s stock market fell steeply on November 20, 2026, and TSMC was one of the major decliners in that broader AI and semiconductor retreat.
 A recent U.S. export-control update expanded government oversight for advanced-node chip fabricators and packagers, adding another policy overhang for companies exposed to leading-edge semiconductor production.
 This weakness came despite strong recent operating data: TSMC said October 2026 revenue rose 14.7% month over month and 59.7% year over year to about NT$586.89 billion.
 TSMC’s third-quarter results were also solid, with revenue of NT$1.49 trillion and diluted EPS of NT$29.43, suggesting today’s move is more about risk sentiment and regulation than a deterioration in the latest reported fundamentals.
 Sources: 
 TSMC, Federal Register, Yahoo Finance
